## Primary-source research and semantic-overlap decision

- **Reader question:** why might a background-monitor process have a nonzero `cpu_percent` with zero `cpu_ms`, why can CPU% exceed 100, and what happens if a PID is reused?
- **Exact source:** [process snapshot arithmetic](https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/blob/c1574366122a90c451bca6a84713e28813ab95e2/agentsight-capture/src/sources/proc.rs) and [monitor samples, SQLite fields and ranking](https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/blob/c1574366122a90c451bca6a84713e28813ab95e2/collector/src/cmd_monitor.rs). Release: [v1.0.35](https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/releases/tag/v1.0.35).
- **Distinct information gain:** source code compares `starttime_ticks` for CPU-ms deltas, but the CPU% previous-snapshot match uses only PID. Its first-sample fallback uses lifetime average CPU rate while CPU-ms returns zero. The monitor I/O delta instead keys by PID plus start time. This creates a reproducible code-level PID-reuse risk, not an asserted production incident. A source-derived nine-case interpretation matrix also covers multi-core percentage, RSS family sums and detailed sampling.
- **Overlap audit:** `/blog/how-agentsight-background-monitoring-works/` owns sampling cadence and storage. `/blog/what-agentsight-process-exit-codes-mean/` owns Linux exit-status evidence. Neither explains the numeric CPU formula or differing process-identity guards. New canonical `/blog/why-agentsight-monitor-cpu-percent-differs/` answers that distinct decision and links both related pages. No manufactured measurements or customer data.
- **Coherent rendered scope:** one new TechArticle, its Blog index/CollectionPage entry, and sitemap entry. Site-wide header, routes, product positioning, existing articles, analytics, workflows, protected controls, and submodule remain untouched. Product documentation remains at `eunomia.dev/agentsight/`. Rollback point: `67c94e8d8034eee7ee3bad2c28733b8e309dbdbe`.
- **Public acceptance:** exact-source `Publish static site` succeeds, deployed `site/.source-sha` equals the squash commit; generated and live article have canonical/H1/TechArticle, Blog index links it, sitemap contains it, and homepage and one older technical article remain available. A reader-cache limitation must be recorded accurately; do not classify unreadable direct fetch alone as an outage.
